spec.description: CMU's package-delivery quadcopter, 209 flights, every second of them in the browser: filter by route, payload, speed, energy and wind and watch the map, the energy charts and the totals follow; replay one on the fleet layer with a timeline that drives the drone and its height, speed, power and voltage.

options.content:
### One delivery drone, 209 flights

Carnegie Mellon flew a **DJI Matrice 100** quadcopter autonomously around Pittsburgh between April and October 2019 to measure what a small-package delivery costs in energy. Each flight was set up with a **route**, a **commanded speed**, a **payload** and a **cruise altitude**; the drone logged its GPS position, orientation, battery voltage and current and the wind (from an anemometer on board) about five times a second.

**Every flight** puts all of them in your browser, one row per second. Pick a route, a payload or a speed on the left, or brush a chart: the map, the charts, the totals and the table follow at once. The map flies every second at its real height, coloured by battery power; **click a point** to replay its flight below. **The picked flight** replays one on the fleet layer: press play on its timeline, or brush a stretch of the flight on the timeline or the curves, and the drone, its trail and the energy used in that window follow.

It is one drone, not a fleet: every flight here is the same aircraft. Data: Rodrigues, Patrikar, Choudhry, Feldgoise, Arcot, Gahlaut, Lau, Moon, Wagner, Matthews, Scherer and Samaras, *In-flight positional and energy use data set of a DJI Matrice 100 quadcopter for small package delivery*, Scientific Data 8, 155 (2021) — [KiltHub](https://kilthub.cmu.edu/articles/dataset/Data_Collected_with_Package_Delivery_Quadcopter_Drone/12683453), CC BY 4.0. The server reads the 107 MB file once a month through the gateway's cache and sends the browser one row per second (38,820 rows); everything after that runs in DuckDB in your browser (Chaski), drawn by Mosaic and Kepler.

spec.rawSql:
SELECT flight::INTEGER AS "Flight", takeoff AS "Take-off", route AS "Route", speed_ms AS "Speed",
       payload_g::INTEGER AS "Payload", altitude_m AS "Altitude", duration_s AS "Duration",
       distance_m AS "Distance", energy_wh AS "Energy", wh_per_km AS "Energy per km",
       wind_ms AS "Mean wind", max_height_m AS "Highest"
FROM $flights
WHERE $__crossfilter($droneFilters)
ORDER BY flight

spec.description: Click a row to show that flight above. Routes: R1 is the main delivery loop (most flights); R2 to R7 other loops; A1 to A3 altitude tests and H hovering, which barely move. Altitude: the commanded cruise altitude.
spec.title: Flights kept

spec.description: What each flight was set up with, and its energy, wind and day. Click a value to keep it (Shift-click to add), drag across a histogram to keep a range: every panel of this row follows, and the counts here show what each pick would leave.
spec.title: Filters

spec.rawSql:
SELECT count(*)::DOUBLE AS flights
FROM $flights WHERE $__crossfilter($droneFilters)

SELECT sum(duration_s) AS seconds
FROM $flights WHERE $__crossfilter($droneFilters)

spec.description: Their flight time, take-off to landing, added up.
spec.title: Time aloft

spec.rawSql:
SELECT sum(distance_m) / 1000 AS km
FROM $flights WHERE $__crossfilter($droneFilters)

spec.description: Their distance flown, from the GPS fixes.
spec.title: Distance

spec.rawSql:
SELECT sum(energy_wh) AS wh
FROM $flights WHERE $__crossfilter($droneFilters)

spec.description: The battery energy they used, take-offs and landings included.
spec.title: Energy

spec.rawSql:
SELECT sum(energy_wh) / nullif(sum(distance_m) / 1000, 0) AS wh_km
FROM $flights WHERE $__crossfilter($droneFilters) AND wh_per_km IS NOT NULL

spec.description: Energy over distance of the flights that cruised (hover and altitude tests barely move).
spec.title: Per km

spec.rawSql:
-- Every second of the flights with a position, at its height over the take-off
-- point. The filters reach the map through its Mosaic selection and it filters
-- on the GPU, with no query in between: the flight's columns are here for that.
-- `time` (since take-off) keeps the panel from renaming `takeoff` to `time`.
SELECT flight::INTEGER AS flight, time, elapsed_s, latitude, longitude, height_m AS altitude,
       power_w, speed_kmh, takeoff, route, payload, cmd_speed, cruise, wind_ms, wh_per_km
FROM $fixes
WHERE latitude IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY flight, elapsed_s

spec.description: One point per second flown, at its height over the take-off point, coloured by battery power: climbs burn the most. Most flights fly route R1, so its shape is drawn many times over. Click a point to replay its flight below.
spec.title: Every second of the flights kept, by battery power

spec.description: Each flight that cruised, at the speed it was commanded (spread a little so they do not hide each other). Faster costs less per kilometre: the trip is shorter and the rotors work in cleaner air. Brush up or down to keep an energy range.
spec.title: Energy per km against commanded speed

- param: picked

options.spec:
# One dot per flight that cruised, coloured by payload (grey: every flight; in
# colour: those the filters keep; ringed: the picked one). Brush up or down to keep an energy range.
params:
  droneFilters: { select: crossfilter }
  picked: { select: intersect }
vconcat:
  - legend: color
    for: by_speed
  - name: by_speed
    plot:
      - mark: dot
        data: { from: flights }
        x: speed_jitter
        y: wh_per_km
        fill: 'rgba(128, 128, 128, 0.25)'
        r: 3.5
      - mark: dot
        data: { from: flights, filterBy: $droneFilters }
        x: speed_jitter
        y: wh_per_km
        fill: payload
        fillOpacity: 0.85
        r: 3.5
      - mark: dot
        data: { from: flights, filterBy: $picked }
        x: speed_jitter
        y: wh_per_km
        stroke: '#00E5FF'
        strokeWidth: 2.5
        r: 7
      - select: intervalY
        as: $droneFilters
        brush: { fillOpacity: 0.06, stroke: currentColor, strokeOpacity: 0.6 }
    xDomain: [3, 13]
    yDomain: [20, 80]
    xLabel: Commanded speed (m/s) →
    yLabel: ↑ Energy per km (Wh/km)
    marginLeft: 44
    colorDomain: [No payload, 250 g, 500 g, 750 g]
    colorRange: ['#73BF69', '#FADE2A', '#F2495C', '#B877D9']
options.variables:
- param: droneFilters
  column: wh_per_km
  from: whkm_lo
  to: whkm_hi

spec.rawSql:
-- The picked flight, second by second: a query of this panel, not a dataset, so
-- picking another flight reloads nothing else. `drone` is the fleet layer's
-- asset and `type` gives it the drone silhouette; `time` is the time since
-- take-off (see the dataset's SQL), on which the timeline's window lands.
SELECT time, elapsed_s, 'M100' AS drone, 'drone' AS type,
       latitude, longitude, height_m, heading, speed_kmh, power_w, voltage_v,
       round(sum(wh) OVER (ORDER BY elapsed_s), 2) AS energy_wh
FROM $fixes
WHERE flight = ${flight:raw}
ORDER BY elapsed_s

spec.description: The picked flight on the fleet layer: the drone at its real height, turned to its heading, with its trail coloured by battery power. It follows the timeline and the curves: the drone stands at the end of the window they hold.
spec.title: Flight replay
Delivery drone flights

query.rawSql:
-- Server side, once per visit: every flight of CMU's package-delivery
-- quadcopter (DJI Matrice 100, Pittsburgh, April to October 2019; KiltHub,
-- CC BY 4.0), one row per second flown, read through the gateway's month-long
-- cache of flights.csv (about 258,000 fixes at ~5 Hz become 38,820 seconds).
-- Each second keeps the energy and the distance flown in it (battery voltage ×
-- current over each step, haversine between fixes), so sums over seconds are
-- the flight's own. Each row also carries what its flight was set up with and
-- the flight's totals: the filters pick flights, and the map and the charts of
-- seconds follow them. Nine altitude tests (A1–A3) logged no GPS, so they have
-- no position. Heading is the yaw of the orientation quaternion as a compass
-- bearing (it matches the GPS course in cruise), at the end of the second.
WITH r AS (
  SELECT flight, time AS t,
         CASE WHEN position_x <> 0 THEN position_x END AS lon,
         CASE WHEN position_y <> 0 THEN position_y END AS lat,
         position_z AS z, battery_voltage AS volts, battery_voltage * battery_current AS w, wind_speed,
         sqrt(velocity_x * velocity_x + velocity_y * velocity_y) AS v,
         (360 - degrees(atan2(2 * (orientation_w * orientation_z + orientation_x * orientation_y),
                              1 - 2 * (orientation_y * orientation_y + orientation_z * orientation_z)))) % 360 AS yaw,
         speed, payload, altitude, route, date, time_day
  FROM read_csv('http://feeds/figshare/files/26385151', types = {'altitude': 'VARCHAR'})
),
s AS (
  SELECT *,
    coalesce(t - lag(t) OVER f, 0) AS dt,
    coalesce(2 * 6371000 * asin(sqrt(
      pow(sin(radians(lat - lag(lat) OVER f) / 2), 2) +
      cos(radians(lat)) * cos(radians(lag(lat) OVER f)) * pow(sin(radians(lon - lag(lon) OVER f) / 2), 2))), 0) AS dm,
    z - first(z) OVER f AS h
  FROM r WINDOW f AS (PARTITION BY flight ORDER BY t)
),
sec AS (
  SELECT flight, floor(t)::INTEGER AS elapsed_s,
    avg(lat) AS latitude, avg(lon) AS longitude, avg(h) AS height_m, max(h) AS top_m,
    avg(v) * 3.6 AS speed_kmh, avg(w) AS power_w, avg(volts) AS voltage_v, arg_max(yaw, t) AS heading,
    sum(w * dt) / 3600 AS wh, sum(dm) AS m, avg(wind_speed) AS wind, max(t) AS tmax,
    any_value(speed) AS speed_ms, any_value(payload) AS payload_g, any_value(altitude) AS altitude_m,
    any_value(route) AS route, any_value(date) AS date, any_value(time_day) AS time_day
  FROM s GROUP BY ALL
)
SELECT
  flight, elapsed_s,
  -- `time` is the time since take-off, counted from midnight on 1 January 2000
  -- (UTC): the same clock for every flight, so a window held on the timeline keeps
  -- its meaning when another flight is picked (the first 30 s are a take-off on
  -- any flight). `takeoff` is when the flight took off, in UTC.
  TIMESTAMP '2000-01-01' + to_seconds(elapsed_s) AS time,
  timezone('UTC', timezone('America/New_York', date + CAST(time_day AS TIME))) AS takeoff,
  strftime(date + CAST(time_day AS TIME), '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M') AS takeoff_local,
  route,
  speed_ms, speed_ms::INTEGER || ' m/s' AS cmd_speed,
  payload_g::INTEGER AS payload_g,
  CASE WHEN payload_g = 0 THEN 'No payload' ELSE payload_g::INTEGER || ' g' END AS payload,
  altitude_m, altitude_m || ' m' AS cruise,
  round(latitude, 7) AS latitude, round(longitude, 7) AS longitude,
  round(height_m, 1) AS height_m, round(speed_kmh, 1) AS speed_kmh, round(power_w) AS power_w,
  round(voltage_v, 2) AS voltage_v, round(heading) AS heading,
  wh, m,
  round(max(tmax) OVER g) AS duration_s,
  -- Hover and altitude tests (speed 0) barely move: no Wh/km for them.
  CASE WHEN speed_ms > 0 THEN round(sum(wh) OVER g / (sum(m) OVER g / 1000), 1) END AS wh_per_km,
  round(avg(wind) OVER g, 1) AS wind_ms,
  round(max(top_m) OVER g) AS max_height_m
FROM sec WINDOW g AS (PARTITION BY flight)
ORDER BY flight, elapsed_s

source.sql:
-- In your browser: one row per flight, from its seconds. What it was set up
-- with (route, commanded speed, payload, cruise altitude), its take-off and its
-- totals.
-- `speed_jitter` spreads the flights at one commanded speed a little apart, so
-- that on the chart they do not hide each other.
SELECT flight,
  any_value(takeoff) AS takeoff, any_value(takeoff_local) AS takeoff_local, any_value(route) AS route,
  any_value(speed_ms) AS speed_ms, any_value(cmd_speed) AS cmd_speed,
  any_value(payload_g) AS payload_g, any_value(payload) AS payload,
  any_value(altitude_m) AS altitude_m, any_value(cruise) AS cruise,
  any_value(duration_s) AS duration_s,
  round(sum(m)) AS distance_m, round(sum(wh), 1) AS energy_wh,
  any_value(wh_per_km) AS wh_per_km, any_value(wind_ms) AS wind_ms,
  any_value(max_height_m) AS max_height_m,
  any_value(speed_ms) + ((flight::INTEGER * 37) % 11 - 5) * 0.09 AS speed_jitter
FROM $fixes
GROUP BY flight
ORDER BY flight

spec.sql:
-- Every flight, labelled by what was set for it: route, commanded speed,
-- payload and cruise altitude.
SELECT flight::INTEGER::VARCHAR AS value,
       '#' || flight::INTEGER || ' · ' || route || ' · ' || speed_ms::INTEGER || ' m/s · '
         || payload_g::INTEGER || ' g · ' || altitude_m || ' m' AS text
FROM $flights ORDER BY flight
SELECT DISTINCT route AS value FROM $flights WHERE route IS NOT NULL ORDER BY 1
SELECT DISTINCT payload AS value FROM $flights WHERE payload IS NOT NULL ORDER BY 1
SELECT DISTINCT cmd_speed AS value FROM $flights WHERE cmd_speed IS NOT NULL ORDER BY 1
SELECT DISTINCT cruise AS value FROM $flights WHERE cruise IS NOT NULL ORDER BY 1
